headline: OpenAI launches ChatGPT desktop app for Linux, now available worldwide
summary: After months of requests from the open-source community, OpenAI has released a dedicated ChatGPT app for Linux users, expanding its reach to all major desktop operating systems.
details: OpenAI has officially launched a dedicated ChatGPT desktop application for Linux users, fulfilling a long-standing request from the open-source community. This release marks the expansion of ChatGPT and Codex across every major desktop operating system.
The new app, currently in preview, offers Linux users access to ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, and Codex. It is available worldwide as of Tuesday.

OpenAI has confirmed support for several popular Linux distributions, including Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04 LTS, Debian 13, and Fedora 43 and 44. These distributions serve as bases for many other downstream "flavors" which are also expected to be compatible.
This move comes shortly after Anthropic released its Claude desktop app for Linux about a month prior, which supports Ubuntu 22.04+ and Debian 12+.
caption:
OpenAI has finally released a dedicated ChatGPT desktop app for Linux users, expanding its reach to all major operating systems.

OpenAI has officially launched a dedicated ChatGPT desktop application for Linux users, fulfilling a long-standing request from the open-source community. This release marks the expansion of ChatGPT and Codex across every major desktop operating system.

The new app, currently in preview, offers Linux users access to ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, and Codex. It is available worldwide as of Tuesday.

OpenAI has confirmed support for several popular Linux distributions, including Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04 LTS, Debian 13, and Fedora 43 and 44. These distributions serve as bases for many other downstream "flavors" which are also expected to be compatible.

This move comes shortly after Anthropic released its Claude desktop app for Linux about a month prior, which supports Ubuntu 22.04+ and Debian 12+.
